# Meet the WCAG 2.2 AA floor in dense UI

Compact interfaces still meet WCAG 2.2 AA: 24 by 24 CSS pixel targets, focus never hidden, 3:1 contrast for controls and meaningful graphics, dismissible hover content, no meaning carried by color alone, and an alternative to every drag.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. Density is where these criteria fail first: small icon targets, sticky chrome covering focus, faint borders, and color-only status. APCA is advisory only and WCAG 3 is still a draft, so WCAG 2.2 AA remains the floor.

## Prefer

- Give every target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or enough spacing that a 24 pixel circle around it overlaps no other target (2.5.8).
- Keep the focused element at least partly visible past sticky headers, toolbars, and overlays (2.4.11).
- Give control boundaries, focus indicators, and meaningful icons 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors (1.4.11).
- Make hover and focus content dismissible without moving focus, hoverable, and persistent until dismissed (1.4.13).
- Pair color with text, shape, or an icon for status and state (1.4.1).
- Offer a single-pointer alternative to every drag (2.5.7).

## Avoid

- Shrinking hit areas to the visible glyph in dense rows.
- Faint borders or icons as the only cue for a control.
- Red and green dots as the only status signal.
- Treating APCA scores or WCAG 3 drafts as a substitute for WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Use when

- Any interactive web or desktop product surface, especially compact rows, toolbars, and icon-only actions.

## Do not use when

- A target is inline in text, its size is set by the user agent, or a specific WCAG exception applies; name the exception.

## Sources

- WCAG 2.2 — https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
- Understanding SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html
- WCAG 3 is not ready yet (on APCA and WCAG 3 status) — https://yatil.net/blog/wcag-3-is-not-ready-yet

## Check

- Is every target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or adequately spaced?
- Does sticky or overlay chrome ever fully cover the focused element?
- Do controls, focus rings, and meaningful icons reach 3:1 non-text contrast?
- Is hover or focus content dismissible, hoverable, and persistent?
- Does any state rely on color alone, and does every drag have a single-pointer alternative?
